claims.statement: The Met describes an identifiable Etruscan language around 700 BCE and cultural flourishing through the end of the second century BCE.
Metal-rich Etruria supported skilled bronze workers whose products circulated around the Mediterranean.

evidence.locator: Opening prose paragraphs on Villanovan chronology, Etruscan culture and metalwork
evidence.note: Broad cultural context, not the lifetime of a unified state or every Etruscan city. The end is a rounded century boundary from the source. No historical territory is reconstructed.
